purpose: Check whether reducing instrument/shelf contact stiffness changes the matched scripted cecum inversion after the reset-contact fix.
interpretation: Reducing the configured rigid tool/shelf ShapeConfig contact ke by 10x did not prevent failure and slightly worsened the most negative signed-volume ratio while slightly reducing the uncalibrated force channel. Because the solver trajectory changed, this is a matched-seed parameter probe, not a paired identical-action causal ablation. A previous seed-0 1000 N/m probe also inverted cecum. Do not tune stiffness to obtain a healthy metric without independent force-displacement calibration.
limits: One seed, one scene, one scripted approach; no statistical or held-out claim.
The contact force channel and tissue mechanics are uncalibrated.
Changing contact stiffness changes the closed-loop trajectory, so output differences combine contact law and path differences.
A positive volume-only outcome would still not validate realistic contact or deformation.
privacy: Tracked record contains aggregate metrics and local ignored-run references only. Source data, frames, credentials, and personal information remain local.
